Hi Kim / Ben —

Acme legal sent back another round on indemnity and we need to lock down a concise internal decision matrix before we reply. Key open items from procurement/legal:
- Who defends third-party IP claims for AI-generated output vs. claims related to customer data ingestion
- Notice windows and evidence preservation custody (they want 10 business days for preservation acknowledgement)
- Insurance offsets and whether we require their insurance to be primary for IP claims
- OSS/data-carveout language (Acme pushed for broader carveouts)

I attached our redline (ACME_MSA_redline_v3.docx). Can you:
1) confirm preferred defend-vs-reimburse approach for third-party AI output claims and a short rationale we can share with procurement;
2) confirm recommended notice/evidence timelines we can commit to operationally; and
3) highlight any hard stops (e.g., indemnity cap thresholds, escrow/escrow triggers, or insurance minimums) we should keep as non-negotiable.

Timing: Acme asked for a response by COB Friday PST. If we can get a 1–2 paragraph decision matrix + a marked paragraph they can copy into their counter, that should help speed things.

Thanks — I can take point on coordination with procurement once we have the matrix.

Neha —

Thanks for sending. A few clarifying questions from procurement/legal so we can evaluate your proposal:

1) For third-party IP claims tied to model output (e.g., a downstream user alleges output infringes a patent), does Redwood take on defense and indemnity regardless of whether the prompt included customer data? Or do you distinguish between: (A) model-only output, (B) output generated from customer-provided protected content, and (C) output that reproduces a third party's preexisting work?

2) Evidence custody: we typically need the vendor to acknowledge preservation within 10 business days of notice and provide a named evidence custodian. Can Redwood meet that operational SLA? If not, what is the expected acknowledgement window?

3) Insurance: does your indemnity trigger require Acme to maintain a particular insurance layer? We usually ask for vendor to have primary coverage for IP claims or specify how offsets apply — please confirm your stance.

4) OSS carveouts: Acme requests that any open-source model training data attribution/claims fall outside vendor indemnity if the claim arises from upstream OSS licensor enforcement. Is that something Redwood can agree to with a limited carveout?

If you can answer inline and/or provide the short decision matrix Neha requested that would be great — we can then route to procurement counsel and circle back.

Best

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Neha / Ben —

Quick take and a draft matrix you can forward to Lara and Evan. High level first: we should keep Redwood responsiblity for third-party claims that arise from our model architecture, core weights, or our training/data pipelines (i.e., model-origin claims). For claims tied to customer-supplied inputs or outputs that reproduce customer-provided protected content, responsibility should be the customer's. We then propose the following decision matrix (concise, copy/paste friendly):

Decision matrix (short, for Acme):
- Scenario A — Claim alleges infringement by the model itself (no customer-supplied content): Redwood = defend & indemnify (Redwood pays defense costs and settlement).
- Scenario B — Claim alleges infringement based on Customer-supplied proprietary input/content used to generate output: Customer = defend & indemnify (customer retains responsibility).
- Scenario C — Claim alleges reproduction of third-party preexisting work discovered in customer inputs or uploaded datasets: Customer = defend & indemnify, unless Redwood had prior written knowledge of the specific dataset and agreed in writing to assume risk.
- Scenario D — Claim is mixed or ambiguous: parties will meet within 10 business days of notice to agree triage; if unresolved after 30 days, Redwood will assume defense pending final rights determination (subject to reimbursement adjustment if customer later establishes responsibility).

Operational answers to Acme's questions:
- Evidence custody/acknowledgement: Redwood can acknowledge preservation within 5 business days and will provide a named evidence custodian. We will aim to preserve relevant logs/KV-cache snapshots for 30 days from notice (longer preservation can be scoped separately). See attached evidence-preservation-plan.pdf for runbook and expected artifacts.
- Insurance: Redwood requires customers maintain commercially reasonable cyber/tech liability insurance for contractual offsets; Redwood will carry primary vendor insurance with $5M per-occurrence for IP and tech liability. Offsets: claims covered by Redwood indemnity are paid by Redwood subject to the cap in the order form; insurance proceeds will be applied in accordance with standard offset language.
- OSS carveouts: we can accept a narrow OSS carveout limited to claims arising solely from upstream licensor enforcement against upstream OSS (i.e., not for cases where model training pipelines introduced third-party proprietary content without attribution). We will not accept a carveout that swallows model-origin claims.

Hard stops and recommended language:
- Cap: keep our proposed cap at 3x the annual subscription fees or $3M, whichever is higher (we prefer to keep the multiplier approach flexible by use-case).
- Escrow/escrow triggers: we will not agree to an escrow mechanism for IP unless the order form reaches a threshold >$1.5M ARR — otherwise we propose performance bonds which are operationally heavy.
- Notice window: we accept 30 business days from discovery for written notice by customer; Redwood will acknowledge within 5 business days.

Action items (for Neha):
1) Share the short decision matrix text above with Lara/Evan and attach the two documents: ACME_MSA_redline_v3.docx + evidence-preservation-plan.pdf.
2) Ask Acme if they require an insurer certificate now (they often request it on signature) — if yes, we can provide an ACORD within 3 business days post-execution.
3) Confirm OSS carveout wording: I can propose a one-paragraph carveout limited to upstream licensor enforcement and exclude model-origin exposure.

I kept this succinct so it's easy for procurement to paste into their counter. Happy to refine if Acme pushes back.
